title: Stalemate in mixed positions
outcomes: Names a position as check, checkmate, stalemate or ongoing when pieces and pawns are mixed
Counts the legal moves of every piece, not only the king
Notices before moving that its own move would stalemate the enemy king

steps.text: **Check, checkmate and stalemate** gave you the definitions. Now the positions are mixed, and you must also look **ahead**. Ask two things: is the king attacked, and does the side to move have **any** legal move, with any piece? And before you move, play your candidate in your head and ask the same two questions about the opponent.

steps.caption: White to move. Qe5 looks strong because it boxes the king in.

line.say: The queen covers h2 and the white king covers g1 and g2. Black has no legal move and is not in check: stalemate.

claims.statement: After Qe5 the black king has no legal move.
After Qe5 nothing attacks the black king.

steps.text: **Count every legal move, not only the king's.** A boxed-in king with a pawn that can still move is simply an ongoing game. The drawn result needs **no legal move at all** and no check. When you are the stronger side, a move that boxes in the king is dangerous exactly when the opponent has nothing else to move.

steps.title: Same queen, one change
steps.prompt: A black pawn appears on a7. Predict first: is the game still drawn?
In the silent round, which answers came from counting every black move, and which from a first glance? Rate how sure you were overall. (low / medium / high)
